title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of THREE questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read the case study carefully before answering Question 2.
Write in full sentences where explanations are required.

questions.prompt: Which communication style respects both your own and other people's rights?

Match each term to its meaning.

context.title: Case study: Lerato's choice
context.text: Lerato (14) has just moved to a new school. A popular group invites her to a party on Friday night. At the party, the group passes around a vape and some alcohol. One of the girls says, 'Come on, everyone does it. Don't be boring.' Lerato wants to be accepted, but she has a netball trial early on Saturday morning and she has promised herself that she will not drink or smoke.

questions.prompt: Identify the type of peer pressure Lerato faces and give a reason.
questions.memo:
✓ Negative peer pressure (1)
✓ She is being pressured to vape and drink, which is harmful (1)

questions.prompt: Write an assertive response Lerato could give.
questions.memo:
✓ Says no clearly (1)
✓ Gives a reason or uses an I-statement (1)
✓ Is respectful / suggests an alternative (1)

questions.prompt: Describe THREE possible consequences if Lerato gives in.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): poor performance at trial; health effects; addiction risk; risky behaviour/unsafe situations; breaking own values/guilt; trouble with parents or the law

questions.prompt: How could healthy self-esteem help Lerato in this situation?
questions.memo:
✓ She would value herself and her goals (1)
✓ and be confident enough to say no without needing the group's approval (1)

questions.prompt: Suggest FOUR ways Lerato can make new friends at her school without compromising her values.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): join netball/sports teams; join clubs or societies; talk to classmates with similar interests; volunteer; attend youth groups; be friendly and open

questions.prompt: Choose TWO rights from the Bill of Rights and give the responsibility that goes with each.
questions.memo:
✓ Right 1 (1) ✓ matching responsibility (1)
✓ Right 2 (1) ✓ matching responsibility (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between prejudice and discrimination, and give an example of discrimination.
questions.memo:
✓ Prejudice is a negative attitude or feeling (1)
✓ Discrimination is unfair treatment / action (1)
✓ Example, e.g. refusing someone a job because of race (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how you would use your interests, abilities and values to choose a career. Give an example.
questions.memo:
✓ Interests: what you enjoy (1)
✓ Abilities: what you are good at (1)
✓ Values: what is important to you (1)
✓ Example linking these to a suitable career (1)

questions.prompt: Describe THREE effective study methods.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): summaries; mind maps; mnemonics; flash cards; past papers; SQ3R; teaching someone

questions.prompt: Give THREE benefits of regular physical activity for teenagers.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): healthy heart/lungs; strong muscles and bones; weight control; better sleep and concentration; reduced stress; lower disease risk

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways substance abuse affects a community.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): more crime and violence; road accidents; pressure on health services and police; loss of productive young people; broken families; unemployment

questions.prompt: Name THREE emotional or social changes that teenagers may experience during puberty.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): mood swings; need for independence/privacy; friends become more important; attraction to others; worry about appearance; increased peer pressure
